eval_layout_margin.jobs: the 12 T1 eval-layout jobs: F/F20 (resnet56_s31/s32, resnet20_s31/s32) limit 4252 s (emitted 2126 s); R2 (8 units) limit 3618 s (emitted 1809 s)
eval_layout_margin.why_thin: Why the emitted margins were thin: b4_timeouts.js scales S1's fit-layout time by penult width and rows only. It leaves out confirmation's B = 1000 bootstrap draws (B = 200 in S1) and its 3-5 confirmation-only T1 targets, and no eval layout was timed in S1. Its row factor also divides by the reference dump's 122,500 rows, although S1's discovery run read 88,000 of them (discovery refuses the 34,500 CONFIRMATION_ONLY rows): the rows read grow 1.57x (C/K/F fits), 2.77x (R2 eval) and 3.22x (F/F20 eval), against the rule's 1.13x, 1.87x and 2.19x. The estimates below model that growth per component.
eval_layout_margin.estimate: S1 reference resnet32 fit 323 s = build/taps 102 s + batch 20 s + 26 targets 200 s (7.7 s per target); resnet32 is the t_ref of every F/F20 and R2 eval limit. The bootstrap share of target time is not measured. An operation count (about 21 b4_core.boot_ci calls per target, each draw 25-30 full-length numpy passes) gives about 0.2-0.33 at B = 200; a first count of 0.13 was wrong, so the central share 0.25 is central, not conservative. Estimates from three cost models (the P2 lead's and two reviews'): F/F20 eval about 1310-1370 s at share 0.25 and 1830-1860 s at 0.5; at share 1.0 (all target time bootstrap) about 2750-2960 s. Against the B4b limits: F/F20 eval margin 3.10-3.25x at share 0.25, 2.29-2.32x at 0.5 and 1.44-1.55x at 1.0; R2 eval 3.12-3.73x at 0.25, 2.26-2.75x at 0.5 and 1.46-1.80x at 1.0. No limit is reached at any share up to 1.0. The share-1.0 values: the P2 lead's model re-run (F/F20 2877 s, R2 2306 s) and the first review's (F/F20 by the resnet32 proxy 2834 s, R2 2008-2217 s); the second review's, extrapolated linearly from its 0.25 and 0.5 values (the bootstrap time is linear in B), gives R2 about 2480 s (1.46x) and F/F20 within 2750-2960 s.
eval_layout_margin.estimate_emitted: SUPERSEDED by B4b (against the emitted limits): F/F20 eval margin 1.55-1.62x at share 0.25 and 1.14-1.16x at 0.5; R2 eval 1.56-1.86x at 0.25 and 1.13-1.37x at 0.5. The limit was reached from a share of about 0.6-0.7 for F/F20 (about 0.64 in the P2 lead's model and in the first review's) and about 0.6-0.85 for R2 (about 0.62 in the second review's model, 0.70 in the P2 lead's and 0.74-0.86 across the first review's three units).
eval_layout_margin.wide_c_fits: Next tightest: the six wide C T1 fits (mobilenetv2_x0_75, mobilenetv2_x1_0, repvgg_a1, repvgg_a2, shufflenetv2_x1_0, shufflenetv2_x1_5; limits 3600-3862 s, emitted 1800-1931 s). The width rule scales by penult width only, but their earlier taps are 2.4-3.7x wider than the reference's. Against the B4b limits: margin 3.72-4.28x at share 0.25, 2.96-3.30x at 0.5 and 2.10-2.24x at 1.0 (emitted: 1.86-2.14x, 1.48-1.65x and 1.05-1.12x). Every other job has at least about 4.6x at share 0.25 in the P2 lead's model (emitted: about 2.3x).
eval_layout_margin.load: S1's t_ref values come from a lane of 4 probes at once (P = 4: no timeouts.json existed at P1, so b4_P used the default 4 GB peak), niced beside the GPU chain and the trainings. Within S1 the same probe's per-target time varied with load: median 5.8 s per target for the 18 T1 fits started 07:03-07:26, 7.6-7.7 s for the four started 07:28-07:30 (resnet32 among them); the supplement's ShuffleNet fit on an idle pod took 5.1 s. S2 runs P = min(quota - 1, free memory / 2.1 GB) probes, up to 16 on a 2x4090, without trainings, so S2's per-job speed is not established to be better than S1's. Under B4b the smallest margin at share 0.5 (about 2.26x) exceeds this 1.3-1.5x load effect combined with a host about 13% slower per core (about 1.7x).
eval_layout_margin.risk_accepted: SUPERSEDED by B4b (written for the emitted limits; kept for the record): A limit cannot be raised after S2 has unsealed (a P2 change outside D8). Two things protect the thin margins. (1) The host: RUN_REQUEST_S2.md section 2 keeps only an EPYC-Genoa-class CPU, S1's class, because a host about 13% slower per core can cross the tightest eval-layout margin at a share of 0.5. (2) D10's relaunch: a job killed by its limit (exit 124) is rerun once under the next S2 tag with unchanged code and timeouts.json; every job that already wrote its output refuses (touched-once) before opening a dump, so the killed job runs almost alone, and the 1.3-1.5x load effect seen in S1 exceeds these margins. Only a job killed in that relaunch too leaves its unit NOT_EVALUABLE for the claims that need the output (R needs 3 of 4 F/F20 units).
eval_layout_margin.risk_after_b4b: A limit still cannot be raised after S2 has unsealed (a P2 change outside D8); B4b raised them at P2, before anything sealed was opened. What protects the margins now: (1) the doubled limits above; (2) the host: RUN_REQUEST_S2.md section 2 keeps only an EPYC-Genoa-class CPU, S1's class, on which the t_ref values were measured (under B4b a host about 13% slower per core crosses no modelled margin); (3) D10's relaunch: a job killed by its limit (exit 124) is rerun once under the next S2 tag with unchanged code and timeouts.json, and every job that already wrote its output refuses (touched-once) before opening a dump, so the killed job runs almost alone. Only a job killed in that relaunch too leaves its unit NOT_EVALUABLE for the claims that need the output (R needs 3 of 4 F/F20 units).

disclosed: T1 X3-3 (ACTIVE; disclosed, not withdrawn), a validity concern about the harm reference: t_harm is the first frame at or after onset where the trailing 64-frame error exceeds the CAL clean error by 5 pt (scripts/t1_streams.py, loss_pt 5, win 64), and the first alarm is never before onset, so on every stream the lead is at most t_harm - onset: a unit's median lead is capped by median(t_harm - onset), which only an alarm at onset reaches. On discovery this cap, read from the stuck detector (it raises no alarm on these two ramps, so the cap is its lead_median + 1800), is 93.5 / 132.5 / 108.5 frames on motion_blur and 115 / 215.5 / 165.5 on defocus_blur for resnet20_hub / resnet56_hub / resnet56_e40. So resnet20_hub cannot reach 100 on motion_blur with any detector, and the other two would need a median alarm within about 32 and 8 frames of onset, when the ramp's corrupted-frame probability is about 11% and 3%. The cap is mostly sampling noise: over 64 frames the 5-pt line is an integer error count (7, 8 or 9 at the units' CAL errors of 4.9-8.9%), and i.i.d. clean frames alone cross it at a median of 113-172 frames after onset at the three STdisc CAL errors and 117-373 frames at those of the six STconf units readable in discovery (Monte Carlo with a 32-bit generator, 20,000 streams per unit). A confirmation SUPPORTED is therefore not impossible, but the label can turn more on each unit's clean error and on that integer threshold than on the detector, which is not what X3-3 was registered to test. History: a withdrawal to INFO was drafted at P2 after X3-3's discovery label came out REFUTED (0/3 STdisc units; best early-tap lead +21 frames on motion_blur, mewma_s1end on resnet56_hub; on defocus_blur every detector's lead is negative on all three units, best -21.5). Its first reason, that a median lead of 100 frames is out of reach whatever the detector does, rested on a Monte Carlo whose generator repeated after about 10,000 draws and was shown false in review. The corrected reason above is a real concern, but no P1 rule anticipated it, so the lead kept X3-3 ACTIVE and discloses it here, before any confirmation read. results/b4/SESSION.md must carry this caveat beside the X3-3 label.

T1 X3-8: t1_eval.js (P1) takes the best early-tap AUROC over knnL2/wnorm at stem and s1end plus x4tap_stem; the 'early' bundle of T1_SCOREBOARD 3.4 also has s2end. The frozen list is kept (not a D8 (e) fix): it is the narrower, stricter reading for a claim that early taps win, and the discovery label is REFUTED either way (occlusion disc: best early minus best head -0.05 to -0.30 on every D unit).
